A: Initial OCT panel from a patient with Purtscher retinopathy; caption describes inner retinal hyperreflectivity and subretinal fluid, matching acute Purtscher OCT findings. He was planned on a three-day follow-up, initially followed by a weekly follow-up on topical nepafenac 1% eye drops one drop twice daily for the right eye. At four weeks follow-up, there was a subtle improvement in vision to counting fingers at 2 meters. His visual acuity further improved to 6/20 with refraction (-1.25 dioptric sphere) at 10 weeks follow-up with a marked resolution of Purtscher fleckens. Subhyaloid hemorrhage was resolving on 10 weeks follow-up, while the optic nerve showed mild temporal pallor (Figures 3, 4).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Initial color fundus photograph from a 16-year-old boy with Purtscher retinopathy after severe traffic accident, showing classic ischemic white posterior pole, cotton-wool spots, and intraretinal hemorrhages. B: Follow-up color fundus photograph at one month from the same Purtscher retinopathy patient, showing decreased white lesions and bleeding. C: Microperimetry overlay on a fundus photograph from the same Purtscher retinopathy patient, showing a central scotoma with decreased sensitivity in the fovea.
panels.attribution_text: Hamoudi et al. Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography of Purtscher Retinopathy after Severe Traffic Accident in 16-Year-Old Boy.. Case reports in ophthalmological medicine 2018. doi:10.1155/2018/4318354. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: (Snellen equivalent) on the right eye and 1.0 on the left eye and was unchanged at one-month examination. Six months later, the visual acuity improved to 0.16 on the right eye and was still normal on the left eye. Anterior segment findings and intraocular pressure were normal. Ophthalmoscopy and fundus photo revealed an ischemic white posterior pole with cotton wool spots and intraretinal hemorrhages mainly in the macula and nasally to the optic disc. The white lesions and bleeding decreased already at the one-month visit (Figure 1), and after 6 months, the white lesions were almost resolved.

At follow-up visits the edema decreased significantly on OCT with disruption of the inner retinal layers but also seemingly disrupted ellipsoid zone. In addition, the thickness of the retina was reduced, from 427 microns at onset to 207 microns at 6 months. A manual segmentation of the OCT layers was conducted in order to ensure correct layer identification and thus thickness calculation. Testing of the central visual field by microperimetry showed a central scotoma with decreased sensitivity in the fovea (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'delayed arterial and venous filling, prolonged arterio-venous (A-V) transit time' on fluorescein angiography

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Fundus photograph of a real patient showing multiple fluffy white posterior-pole opacities explicitly captioned as cotton-wool spots in Purtscher-like retinopathy. B: Early-phase FA of the same patient showing delayed filling consistent with the captioned occlusive perfusion abnormality of Purtscher retinopathy. C: Mid-phase FA panel demonstrating the captioned nonperfusion/choroidal dropouts and irregular FAZ of Purtscher retinopathy. D: Late-phase FA showing perivascular staining/leakage and ischemic nonperfusion captioned as part of this patient's Purtscher-like retinopathy.
